title: Mount Outdoor TV with a Purpose-Built Enclosure: Wall mounting a 65-inch TV on an exterior deck

locations.name: Exterior deck wall (shade-side) with clapboard siding; mounting on the wall near a deck area
locations.basis: Transcript references deck, wall, and clapboard siding; mentions studs and mounting to the wall

summary: This Old House presents a practical indoor-to-outdoor TV upgrade by mounting a TV behind a purpose-built outdoor enclosure on an exterior wall of a shaded deck. The host team weighs sun exposure, selects a wall suitable for mounting, and sizes for a 65-inch screen. They replace an indoor TV setup with an enclosure that includes cooling fans, thermostats, and optional humidity/heat controls, and they implement a behind-the-TV receptacle with weatherproof, tamper-resistant hardware fed from a dedicated outdoor-rated circuit protected by an AFCI/GFCI breaker. The process covers spacing the TV on foam blocks inside the enclosure, aligning and bolting the enclosure to wall studs, routing and sealing power cords, and sealing mounting interfaces with silicone to maintain a watertight install. The project concludes with wiring, a final power test, and a demonstration that the TV returns a live signal on the new outdoor setup.
topics: Foam mounting blocks provided by enclosure
Sealing with putty around electrical box

sections.title: Plan and wall considerations
concepts: relocating from indoor to outdoor viewing
shade vs sun exposure on deck
preference for wall mounting to avoid hazards
sections.description: Heath and Joanna discuss the problem of dragging an indoor TV outdoors and evaluate sun/shade conditions, concluding that mounting on a shaded exterior wall is preferable to reduce tripping risk and weather exposure.

sections.title: Outdoor enclosure rationale
sections.description: They introduce the outdoor TV enclosure as a flexible, protective alternative to an all-in-one outdoor TV, noting the enclosure brings the benefits of outdoor-ready tech without the high cost of a purpose-built outdoor TV.

sections.title: TV prep inside enclosure
concepts: foam mounting blocks from enclosure manufacturer
spacing around the frame for mounting hardware
raising the TV for bracket clearance
sections.description: The TV is prepared with foam blocks provided by the enclosure maker to create the necessary clearance and support before sliding the enclosure over and aligning the mounting hardware.

sections.title: Electrical planning and cord management
concepts: sealed cord entry using a cut-out path
sections.description: They plan how to route power inside the enclosure, install a surge protector, and manage the cord so the entry remains sealed and tidy, improving reliability and accessibility for servicing.

sections.title: Wall placement and mounting height planning
concepts: center the mounting bracket on the housing
sections.description: The team centers the bracket on the enclosure and identifies a wall spot, checking for clearance and stud support to ensure a solid, serviceable mount.

sections.title: Receptacle wiring and final sealing
sections.description: They install a weather-resistant, tamper-resistant receptacle fed by a dual-function AFCI/GFCI breaker, seal the box with putty and silicone, mount the enclosure with lag bolts, and perform a final power test to verify operation.

featured_techniques.technique: Outdoor TV enclosure with integrated cooling fans, thermostats, and humidity/heater options
Use of foam mounting blocks supplied by enclosure manufacturer to provide proper TV support and spacing inside the enclosure
Routing power through a dedicated surge protector inside the enclosure and using an external conduit/pass-through to keep the area weather-tight
Weather-resistant, tamper-resistant exterior receptacle installed with putty and silicone sealing for waterproofing
Secure mounting to wall studs with lag bolts and seal all mounting penetrations for watertight integrity
